messages:
kai: Heads up — saw a spike of OOMs on staging after switching to the percentile-based workspace sizing. Started after yesterday's deploy. Anyone seen this pattern with long KV contexts?

devon: Which percentile change did we make? dynamic-reserve -> 99p global? any repro? :eyes:

kai: Swapped to 99th-percentile workspace sizing for FFN (to shave costs). It reduced avg footprint but when requests had long KV (seq_len 32 -> 2048) we hit OOMs. Attaching quick profiler excerpt below.

infra-bot: New alert created: PROD-STAGING OOM spike (alert#1930000123) — https://internal/alerts/1930000123 :rotating_light:

maria: Likely cause: heuristic assumed "workspace dominated", but KV cache growth wasn't modeled. So allocations for workspace + KV + cuBLAS temp can exceed slab reservation. Need to fold kv_bytes into the workspace estimator.

samir: Quick numbers from the trace: cuBLASLt GEMM temp ~1.2GB, FlashAttn temp ~600MB, KV cache ~3.5GB (int16), other reserves ~300MB -> total ~5.6GB. Our slab threshold for that worker was 5.0GB -> OOM.

devon: Repro snippet to compute peak estimate I used locally:```python
# pseudo estimate
batch=1
seq=2048
hidden=512
kv_bytes = batch*seq*hidden*2  # int16 KV
ffn_ws = ffn_workspace_est(hidden, batch, seq)
attn_ws = flash_attn_workspace_est(batch, seq, hidden)
total_est = kv_bytes + ffn_ws + attn_ws + static_reserve
print(total_est)
```

sofia: Two immediate mitigations: 1) Make chooser aware of kv_bytes and prefer kernel variants with lower transient scratch when kv_bytes is large. 2) Add a quick precommit probe (simulate allocations without touching CUDA) to predict whether the full set fits. If not, route to smaller kernel / reduce batch / return 429.

kai: The latency tail also regressed for long-context requests (p99 up ~15%). We could accept a small latency/cost bump if it eliminates OOMs, but want minimal impact on short contexts.

maria: Suggest multi-tier rules: 
- if seq <= 512: prefer FlashAttention (best perf)
- if 512 < seq <= 1024: try Triton path with medium scratch
- if seq > 1024 or kv_bytes > kv_threshold: prefer cuBLASLt matmul path (lower temp) or quantized kernels
Also adjust probereserve to add kv_bytes into the probe.

devon: Implementation idea: before kernel selection we run `predict_peak(request_meta)` which returns predicted_peak_bytes. Kernel chooser takes free_gpu_mem and predicted_peak and picks variant with smallest predicted_peak that meets perf/cost policy. If none fit, pick a safe fallback: smaller batch / block decode.

samir: Ran a canary patch locally that: a) accounts for kv_bytes in estimator b) downgrades to cuBLASLt when predicted_peak > 90% slab. Results: p99 latency for long-context down from 420ms -> 360ms, OOMs -> 0 on 500 runs, short-context median latency +3%.

sofia: nice. can we add metric tags for "chooser_reason" so we can slice which requests were routed to fallback? :+1:

kai: I'll open a small PR with the probe + metric tags. Planning a staging canary tonight. Link when ready. Also adding a dashboard to show predicted_peak vs actual peak.

devon: Also we should test with quantized KV (int8) scenarios — estimator needs model/quantization-aware computations.

maria: Agreed. I'll add a unit for the estimator: test cases for seq {32,128,512,1024,2048} x quant {fp16,int8} x batch {1,4}.

kai: Thanks all. Canary push scheduled 22:00 PST. Will monitor histograms and OOM alert. If anyone wants to watch: /run profiler --live staging --thread 1930000123

sofia: :thumbsup: great plan.

samir: If canary looks good i'll promote the patch to prod tune branch.

kai: closing for now — will update thread with PR link and final numbers.
